original_question: For a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in R^3 whose boundary is a planar closed curve C, what hypotheses on the boundary guarantee that the surface lies entirely on one side of the boundary plane, and what additional conclusions hold when C is convex?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.2 in Section 2 (Part I: Circular boundary); the draft’s last clause about the convex case also brushes against the immediately following Problem 2.4.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient space R^3, the class of objects (compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surfaces), the fact that the boundary is a planar closed curve C, the central one-sidedness question relative to the boundary plane, and the paper’s special attention to the convex-boundary case.
missing_details: The paper formulates this as an open problem, not as an established theorem: it asks for conditions on the boundary under which a compact embedded cmc surface spanning a planar closed curve C is contained in one side of the boundary plane.

To make the question stand alone, one should name the plane P containing C and say explicitly that the conclusion sought is that the surface is contained in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by P.
The paper’s notation matters: a surface 'has C as a boundary' when the immersion maps ∂Σ diffeomorphically onto C; this is the implicit meaning of 'spanning C'.

The draft’s phrase 'what additional conclusions hold when C is convex?' is not itself the exact wording of Problem 2.2. In the paper, the convex case is mentioned tersely ('And if C is convex?'), while the separate nearby follow-up Problem 2.4 asks whether, for a simple closed convex curve C in a plane P, a compact embedded cmc surface with ∂Σ = C that lies on one side of P must be a topological disk.

The nearby context includes partial results that the draft omits: Koiso’s partial answer under the extra hypothesis Σ ∩ (P \ D) = emptyset, and the later cited result that if C is convex and Σ is transverse to P along C, then Σ lies on one side of P.

This problem is motivated in the paper as a route toward Problem 2.1 (the circular-boundary version of Alexandrov’s theorem): if one could prove the needed one-sidedness in the circle case, Alexandrov reflection would force a spherical cap.
refined_question: Let C be a planar closed curve contained in a plane P ⊂ R^3, and let Σ ⊂ R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary ∂Σ = C. Under what conditions on the boundary curve C must Σ be contained in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by P? In particular, what can be said when C is convex?
justification: The draft matches Problem 2.2 almost verbatim: the paper asks exactly for boundary conditions forcing a compact embedded cmc surface spanning a planar closed curve C to lie on one side of the boundary plane. The only substantial mismatch is that the draft turns the convex add-on into a request for 'additional conclusions,' whereas the paper treats that convex clause only as part of the same open problem and then moves immediately to a separate convex-boundary follow-up (Problem 2.4). So the narrowest paper-faithful refinement is Problem 2.2 itself, with the convex follow-up noted as adjacent context rather than folded into the main question.
